subject: OrionWorks VPC: elevated tail latency and intermittent 503s - tuning + exec sync requested
messages:
From: Alex Parnell <alex.parnell@orionworks.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@orionworks.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2028 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: High tail latency and 503s on our private cluster

Soojin —

We started seeing a sharp rise in tail latency this morning on our Redwood private deployment (vpc-orion-prod). P95/P99 for text-generation calls has climbed from the usual 150ms/420ms to 1.2s/3.8s and we're also seeing intermittent 503s for approximately 2% of requests during peak windows (US-EAST). Attaching recent logs and a pod listing.

What we've tried so far:
- Rolling restart of the inference pool (no change)
- Scaling up pods by +20% (temporary drop, then recovery to high latency)

Impact: client-facing feature degradation; our SLAs are at risk. We need an engineering-led remediation plan and executive contact if this will take more than 24 hours.

Attachments: orion-prod-logs-20281120.zip, k8s-pod-list-20281120.txt

Thanks,
Alex Parnell
CRO, OrionWorks

Immediate ask from our side:

We’ll aim to produce a short remediation plan within 3–4 hours and propose either a quick config rollback or a targeted hotfix. If this persists past tomorrow morning we’ll request an executive sync to discuss credits and reserve capacity options.

I’ll coordinate a follow-up note with next steps.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2028 19:00:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency and 503s on our private cluster

Soojin / Alex — quick triage notes after looking through the logs and traces:

Findings:
- Intermittent KV cache misses on hot prefixes correlated with p99 spikes (see trace ids in attached logs).
- Several pods show long GC pauses in the tokenizer process and elevated CUDA kernel timeouts on a subset of hosts (approx 12% of the pool).
- Batching config was recently widened to max_batch_size=256 in attempt to improve throughput (last rollout 2028-11-15). That increases variance for short requests.

Immediate remediation (recommended, low-risk order):
1) Reduce max_batch_size from 256 -> 128 to reduce tail amplification for small-sequence requests (runtime config, no deploy).
2) Pin the older kernel variant on the 12% of hosts showing CUDA timeouts (hotpatch) and drain to reprovision nodes flagged with driver's 510 warnings.
3) Increase KV cache size for hot prefixes by +20% for the next 6 hours to assess impact on p99.

If we can apply (1) and (3) now we should see measurable p95/p99 improvements within 30–60 minutes. If not, proceed with (2) which requires node-level maintenance.

I'll prepare a short playbook and a rollback plan. Attaching the initial mitigation playbook.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Inference Engineer — Redwood Inference

- 11:30 ET: Exec sync (OrionWorks CRO + Redwood Head of Sales + SVP of Eng) to review impact and commercial remediation (credits, reserved capacity offer).

Please confirm availability for the 11:30 exec sync. I’ve tentatively booked a 30-minute block — sharing calendar link.

Quick update and confirmed actions:

- 09:05 ET: Reduced max_batch_size to 128 and increased KV cache +20%. Observed p95 drop from ~1.2s -> 310ms and p99 from ~3.8s -> ~720ms within 45 minutes. 503 rate dropped from 2% -> 0.4%.
- Rishi is coordinating kernel pinning for the 12% of affected hosts; ETA for node maintenance and drain: 6 hours (to minimize customer traffic impact).
- Tessa: exec sync scheduled 11:30 ET (calendar invite sent). Please bring finance for potential credit discussion.

- Rishi: complete kernel pin + node reprovision (ETA 21 Nov 15:00 ET).
- Laura: monitor metrics and report any regression to this thread (ongoing).
- Tessa: lead the 11:30 exec call and capture any commercial asks.
- Soojin: follow up with a post-mortem and proposed reserved-capacity recommendation by EOD tomorrow.
